definitions.explanation: The number two thousand. Formed by combining {二|に} (two) and {千|せん} (thousand).

examples.japanese: {二千|にせん}{年|ねん}に{生|う}まれました。
examples.english: I was born in the year two thousand.

examples.japanese: この{町|まち}には{二千|にせん}{人|にん}ぐらい{住|す}んでいます。
examples.english: About two thousand people live in this town.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}まで{二千|にせん}メートルぐらいあります。{歩|ある}いて{二十|にじゅう}{分|ぷん}かかります。
examples.english: It's about two thousand meters to the station. It takes twenty minutes on foot.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}は{二千|にせん}{五百|ごひゃく}{円|えん}です。{少|すこ}し{高|たか}いですが、とても{良|よ}い{本|ほん}です。
examples.english: This book is two thousand five hundred yen. It's a bit expensive, but it's a very good book.

notes: Unlike {三千|さんぜん} (three thousand), which has a voiced consonant, {二千|にせん} keeps the unvoiced せん. Japanese counting follows a pattern where multiples of thousand are [number] + {千|せん}, but 3000 and 8000 have special pronunciations (さんぜん and はっせん).
